llm.summary: The skill's instructions generally match a local Mac-based Naver publishing tool, but the SKILL.md references environment variables, local config files, and fallback admin keys that are not declared — this mismatch and the use of an external npx package are disproportionate and worth questioning before install.

dimensions.detail: Name/description say 'publish to Naver Blog via a buyer-local thin-runner' which matches the runtime flow (local Mac runner, dry_run -> login -> publish_live). However the SKILL.md references control-plane artifacts (CONTROL_PLANE_URL + ACP_ADMIN_API_KEY) and multiple runtime tokens (PROOF_TOKEN, SETUP_URL, OPENCLAW_OFFERING_EXECUTE_URL) that are not declared in the skill metadata. Requiring an ACP admin API key as a fallback is unexpected for a publisher-only tool and looks disproportionate to the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions tell the agent to run npx @y80163442/naver-thin-runner commands, start a local daemon, and auto-load X_LOCAL_TOKEN from ~/.config/naver-thin-runner/config.json. The document therefore expects the agent to interact with local services and a local config file and to accept sensitive tokens, but the skill metadata does not declare these files/vars. The instructions do not explicitly direct collection/exfiltration beyond the publishing flow, but the unspecified token/credential usage gives the agent broad discretion.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (instruction-only), which is lower risk, but runtime commands rely on 'npx @y80163442/naver-thin-runner'. That will fetch and execute code from the npm registry (a scoped package with an unfamiliar namespace). Relying on npx at runtime is a moderate risk; the skill should have declared the package or provided vetted tool files.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Skill metadata declares no required env vars or config paths, yet SKILL.md expects multiple runtime variables and tokens (SETUP_URL or PROOF_TOKEN + SETUP_ISSUE_URL, OPENCLAW_OFFERING_EXECUTE_URL, CONTROL_PLANE_URL + ACP_ADMIN_API_KEY fallback, optional X_LOCAL_TOKEN auto-loaded from ~/.config). Asking for an ACP_ADMIN_API_KEY as a fallback is especially disproportionate for a simple publisher and could grant broad control if actually used.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and there's no install spec that would persist code on-system. The skill expects to interact with a local runner/daemon but does not request permanent, always-on inclusion or modification of other skills. Autonomous invocation is allowed (platform default) but is not combined with 'always:true'.

llm.guidance: This skill appears to implement a local Mac-based publisher, but its SKILL.md mentions several environment variables, tokens, and a local config file that are not declared in the metadata — and it relies on running an npm-scoped package via npx. Before installing or using the skill: (1) Ask the publisher to explicitly list required environment variables and config paths (do not hand over ACP_ADMIN_API_KEY unless you understand why an admin-level key is needed). (2) Request the URL or source for the npm package @y80163442/naver-thin-runner and review its code or a vetted release (npx will fetch and run remote code). (3) If you must run it, do so on an isolated Mac runner where you can perform the one-time login manually and verify the local daemon's behavior; inspect ~/.config/naver-thin-runner/config.json to confirm only expected tokens are present. (4) Prefer a version that declares its required secrets and does not fall back to broad control-plane admin credentials. If the vendor cannot clarify these points, treat the skill as untrusted.
